full_judgment:
This appeal arises out of a suit for declaration of title. The plaintiff's case in brief was that the suit land originally belonged to one Sarat Chandra Roy who sold his interest in the suit property by kabala to defendants Nos. 1 & 2 who again settled the suit land with the plaintiff at a rental of Taka 8/- per annum on 2nd Baisakh, 1352 B. S. In Srabon, 1365 B. S. the plaintiff for the first time came to learn that the R.S. Khatian relating to the suit land had been wrongly recorded in the name of Satish Chandra Roy, the predecessor-in-interest of defendants Nos. 1 & 2 Since the said wrong record has cast a cloud on his title and possession, the plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of his title. 

 2. Defendant No. 6 alone contested the suit by filing a written statement in which he denied the allegation made in the plaint. His case, inter alia was that the story of settlement of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff was a myth and the plaintiff never acquired any right, title or possession in the suit land. His further contention was that the R.S. khatian has been correctly recorded and the defendant had taken settlement of the suit land from defendants 3 to 5 sons of Satish Chandra Roy, the original owner and his name has also been recorded in the S.A. khatian, on the basis of a decree obtained by him in a title suit instituted against defendants Nos. 3 to 5.
